newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Bank of Baroda opens 8.5 bln rupee IPO.
newsitem.headline: India's Bank of Baroda opens 8.5 bln rupee IPO.

text.p: India's state-run Bank of Baroda's 8.5 billion rupee initial public offer opened for subscription on Thursday and most market analysts expect the bank to complete the issue without any problems.
The current slump in the stock market may at most affect the amount of oversubscription, analysts said.
"They have a good brand image within India and among Indians abroad," said an executive at one of the merchant bankers to the maiden issue of India's second largest state-run bank.
The bank is offering 100 million shares of 10 rupees face value at 85 rupees a share.
The funds are being raised to augment the net-worth of the bank for meeting future capital adequacy requirements, to augment long-term resources and to obtain listing on bourses.
The Indian government now owns 100 percent of equity, which will fall to 66 percent after the issue.
It is second only to the State Bank of India in terms of deposits and gross profits, analysts said.
"It has a market share of 7.09 percent among total deposits of public sector banks and a market share of 7.69 percent among total advances of public sector banks," said a banking analyst.
Many security firms have advocated a buy on the IPO.

"Because of the constraints faced by the SBI stock -- which is undervalued but is constrained by the 20 percent FII ceiling -- we believe the Bank of Baroda stock could be an attractive investment and could offer steady returns over the medium term," said Khandwala Securities in a report.
It was referring to a ceiling on the percentage of a firm's total equity that could be bought by foreign institutional investors.

"Good issues, for example from the Hindustan Lever group, have sailed through even in times of stock market slump," said a broker. He said no one expected Bank of Baroda to report poor subscription to its maiden public issue.
